name: Act of March 3, 1873 for the sale of the remaining Miami reserve in Kansas (17 Stat. 631)
promises: Not a treaty. Royce summarises the Act as providing that the remainder of the Miami reserve in Kansas be sold and that the Miami may become merged with the Kaskaskia and others.
Royce describes the remnant as several detached tracts within the outer lines of the 70,000 acres reserved by the treaty of 1854.
today: In Docket 251-A the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma claimed, among other things, an accounting for the sale of slightly more than 10,000 acres of unallotted Kansas land that brought about $80,000. The Commission recorded that the land was sold at appraised value, that there was little basis to challenge the appraisals, and approved a $10,000 compromise on January 9, 1969.

openQuestions: The Docket 251-A compromise does not name the 1873 Act; it is reported here as the closest claim located, not as a finding about this sale. A settlement would count only as litigation in any case.
Docket 251 (1958) concerns the 1854 cession in Kansas, not this remnant.
